record.paper_title: Finite-density lattice QCD and sign problem: current status and open problems
record.original_question: Why does the early-onset problem appear in finite-density lattice QCD, with severe phase fluctuations setting in when the quark chemical potential reaches mπ/2, and how can one reliably study the hadron phase beyond that threshold? In particular, what mechanism explains the onset of extreme difficulty at µ = mπ/2 and how can simulations be extended into the physically relevant dense hadronic regime associated with nuclei and neutron stars?

evidence.quote: Behind the difficulty in the low-temperature region is the early-onset problem: when the quark chemical potential reaches mπ/2 (where mπ is the meson mass) at zero temperature, intense phase fluctuations set in.
Due to the early-onset problem, it is difficult to go beyond µ = mπ/2 by using the gauge configurations generated at µ < mπ/2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider lattice QCD at zero temperature and finite quark chemical potential μ, formulated on a Euclidean spacetime lattice with the standard Wilson or staggered fermion action. The grand-canonical partition function

Z(μ) = ∫ DU det M(U,μ) e^{-S_g(U)}

has a fermion determinant det M(U,μ) that is complex for μ ≠ 0, producing a sign (phase) problem. Empirically, in the cold dense regime one observes the following "early-onset" phenomenon: at zero temperature, as the quark chemical potential μ is increased from 0, severe phase fluctuations of det M(U,μ)/det M(U,0) suddenly set in once μ crosses the threshold μ = m_π/2, where m_π is the pion mass. Consequently, reweighting or any approach that relies on gauge configurations generated at μ = 0 (or at μ < m_π/2) breaks down beyond this threshold, even though the physical baryon onset is expected to occur near μ = m_N/3 ≫ m_π/2 (where m_N is the nucleon mass).

Problem. 
(a) Provide a rigorous mechanism, at the level of the eigenvalue distribution of the Dirac operator M(U,μ) and/or of the phase-quenched (isospin-chemical-potential) theory, that explains why μ = m_π/2 is precisely the threshold at which the sign/phase problem becomes severe in the T → 0 limit, and quantify the rate of growth of the phase fluctuations and of the sign-problem severity for μ > m_π/2.
(b) Devise a simulation algorithm (for example based on complex Langevin dynamics, Lefschetz-thimble integration, density-of-states methods, canonical/fugacity expansions, dual variables, tensor networks, or any other framework) that is provably reliable for full lattice QCD with dynamical light quarks in the cold, dense hadronic regime m_π/2 < μ < m_N/3 and beyond, in the sense of yielding controlled estimates of bulk thermodynamic observables (baryon number density, energy density, equation of state) at zero or sufficiently low temperature, with statistical and systematic errors that do not grow exponentially with the spacetime volume.
artifact.status_search_result: The early-onset/sign problem in cold dense lattice QCD remains open. The general sign problem is known to be NP-hard, and while partial mechanistic understanding exists (spreading of Dirac eigenvalues in the complex plane and the role of pion-pair excitations in the phase-quenched theory explain the μ = m_π/2 threshold), no algorithm reliably simulates full lattice QCD with dynamical light quarks in the cold dense hadronic regime beyond μ = m_π/2 up to and past the nuclear onset μ ≈ m_N/3. Recent (2024) studies in two-color QCD and ongoing work with complex Langevin, Lefschetz thimbles, and density-of-states methods illustrate continued effort, but the problem for QCD itself is unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Finite-density lattice QCD and sign problem: Current status and open problems
status_evidence.claim: The early-onset problem is explicitly listed among current open problems of finite-density lattice QCD.

status_evidence.title: Lattice study on finite density QC2D towards zero temperature
status_evidence.snippet: Studies of two-color QCD as a surrogate avoiding the sign problem.
status_evidence.claim: Ongoing 2024 research uses two-color QCD as a workaround, indicating that the QCD case remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Sign problem in finite density lattice QCD
status_evidence.snippet: Phase fluctuations of the determinant become severe near μ ≈ m_π/2 due to pion-pair contributions.
status_evidence.claim: The mechanism partially explaining the m_π/2 threshold is documented, but no reliable simulation method beyond this threshold exists.
